neighbours.label: 'deaf' / 'hearing' named alongside blindness or sight (blind and deaf; sight and hearing): the second sense in the pair
fire: After the fever the boy was left blind and deaf for the rest of his life.
The school teaches children who are blind or deaf from the surrounding districts.
Old age slowly took away his sight and hearing, but not his humour.
The explosion left two workers blinded and deafened for several hours.
Rubella in pregnancy can cause blindness and deafness in the baby.
She lost her vision and her hearing in the same accident.
The dog is thirteen now, half blind and nearly deaf, but still eats well.
The charity prints books for the blind and runs clubs for the deaf.
quiet: After the fever the boy was left weak and pale for the rest of the winter.
The school teaches children who are blind or partially sighted from the surrounding districts.
Old age slowly took away his strength and appetite, but not his humour.
The explosion left two workers bruised and shaken for several hours.
Rubella in pregnancy can cause heart defects and low weight in the baby.
She lost her wallet and her passport in the same accident.
The dog is thirteen now, half lame and nearly toothless, but still eats well.
The charity prints books for the poor and runs clubs for the elderly.

notes: Probes: 'blind and deaf' 0.54, 'hearing or eyesight' 0.32, 'deaf since birth' (no blindness) 0.21, 'tired and thin' 0.01, 'liver or kidneys' 0.11. The pole also fired on 'electricity, water' 0.38 and the top examples include ' water' and ' air', so it may mark the expected next member of a familiar set more generally; this test covers only the senses.
